# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-218-223 (§§218–223)

Reviewer: adversarial, all 73 units, 418 words. Files read: conventions.md, runbook.md, packet.md, units.json, the shared glossary (6,075 entries), and the pass-1 review of 214-217 for rigor. No modern translation opened or recalled; no web. `gloss.json` (the glosser's) not touched. `units.json` edited in place by script (utf-8, ensure_ascii False, indent 1, as before); original kept in the scratchpad as `units.orig.json`.

Checked by script against the packet: every `t` equals the packet words of its indices (73 units, 418 words, each once, in order); `ln` and `p: true` correct (first unit of §§218, 219, 220, 221, 222, 223 only); the first-morph Ming bracket of every word equals the packet's Ming gloss; every Han string quoted in a note was looked up in the packet's Ming column for that unit (this found two false citations, U18 and U31; the other hits were variant-form characters, 并/幷, 巴徹/巴撒, or deliberate cross-references). Quote marks in `i` were counted against the printed marks: balanced, and every supplied mark is now said in a note (U28 added). Method otherwise: original → `l` word by word; `l` ↔ `i`; `i` rebuilt from the grammar; each morph lemma compared with the glossary's entry for the same token.

Totals: 0 critical, 3 major, 13 moderate, 8 minor (24 changes). `t`, `ln`, `p`, word counts and order untouched.

## Changes

### Major
1. **U15 (§219) · `i`, `n` · major.** `i` made Qada'an a co-doer ("had me tended" by the sons and the daughter) while the note itself, the morph and the glossary read Qadaγ̇an-i as accusative, and asaraγ̇ulžu is a causative: a name in the accusative before a causative converb is the one made to tend, not a doer beside the sons. Done: `i` "Sorqan-Shira, with his own sons Chila'un and Chimbai, having Qada'an, his own daughter, tend (me); hiding (me), staying (with me),"; note says Qada'an is the object of the causative, the doers of the chain are Sorqan-Shira and his sons, and that the person tended and hidden (Temüjin) is unnamed and is my reading. `l` already read "having-caused-to-raise" and was left.
2. **U46 (§220) · `i`, `n` · major.** "Old Shirgötü, Alaq and Naya'a, with their sons": three men plus their sons. The same grouping of names + köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen was read in U15/U21 as "the first name, with his sons (the next two names)", and the glossary already has Alaq as "one of Shirgügetü's sons"; the reflexive -ben (singular possessor) goes with the first name. Done: `i` "Old Shirgötü, with his sons Alaq and Naya'a, together with you, seizing Tarqutai-Kiriltuq for us, as you came,"; the "(to bring him)" gloss, which was not in the Ming, replaced by "for us" (bidan-dur); note now states the grouping, the link with the glossary (and that Shirgötü may be the earlier parts' Shirgügetü), and that why Naya'a is also "you" (ta) is unclear; marked as a reading. Note also now says the Ming alternates 俺/咱 for bida (house, 165-168).
3. **U51 (§220) · `i`, `n` · major.** Same misgrouping ("with their sons"); same fix. Also removed the stray ",." typo in the note.

### Moderate
4. **U2 · `i`, `l`, `n`, morph · moderate.** (a) "being diligent" for kičiġe- against the Ming 謹愼 "careful"; (b) "ready to fight" for qadqulduqu bolun: nothing in the Ming (厮殺的 "fighting"); the glossary's "about to fight" rests on a different Ming (要厮殺); (c) the morph and note left -du- of qadqul-du-qu unaccounted for (the glossary has the reciprocal -du-). Done: `i` "taking care in front of me and being one who fights"; `l` "fighting-one becoming"; morph split qadqul- / -du- reciprocal / -qu; note says what the grammar gives and that what it says of the father is left open.
5. **U3 · morph, `n` · moderate.** Same missing -du- in qadqul-du-qui-dur. Inserted, note amended.
6. **U13, U14 · morph lemma, `n` · moderate.** Lemma naiti- for naitažu / naitaγdamu: the forms are naita-ž-u and naita-γda-mu, and the glossary's naitamu, naitaγdan use naita-. Changed to naita- (words 78 and 83) and in the U14 note.
7. **U14 · `i`, `n` · moderate.** "there (he was told), ‘He is envied by his own brothers,’": "(he was told)" and the quotation marks are invented (no speaker, no marks printed, and the note does not say they are supplied). Done: "and there, saying that he was being envied by his own brothers,"; note says the subject of "is envied" is unmarked and whose words these are cannot be said.
8. **U18 · `n` · moderate.** Note cited the Ming for čeġeži as 胷膈; the packet has 心懷 (the glossary's 胷膈 is from an earlier part). Done: cites 心懷 "heart, bosom" and says the earlier part had 胷膈.
9. **U24 · `n` · moderate.** Said the closing mark ends "the speech opened at Nama-ji"; that speech closed at ta" (U20). The mark at medetügei" closes Sorqan-Shira's speech opened at Sojurγaγ̇asu (U22). Corrected.
10. **U28 · `n` · moderate.** `i` closes the speech with ” though Shiratori prints no mark after orotuγai; his next closing mark is at γuidqun (U36). A supplied mark must be said. Done: note says so, and that `i` reopens at erte (U31).
11. **U33 · morph, `n` · moderate.** Lemma dataγ̇u- invented a second stem beside U36's dutaγ̇u- and the glossary's dutaγ̇u (adj/participle, "from duta-"); the final -i was labelled "participle ending" with no support (dutaγ̇u-juγ̇an has no -i). Done: lemma dutaγ̇u (printed dataγ̇u-); -i "ending (uncertain; perhaps the accusative, perhaps part of the stem)"; note amended.
12. **U37 · morph, `n` · moderate.** Lemma darqa- "free" with plural -d, and a note citing "darqan, the privileged class" (remembered, not in the sources). The glossary's darqad-un is darqan "a free man (Ming 自在)" + -d and says any technical sense of darqan is not in these sources. Done: lemma darqan, gloss and note follow the glossary.
13. **U60 · `i`, `n` · moderate.** "that principle he held a great law": a third person with no support, in a speech whose "his words" (in-ü) are Naya'a's and which ends with the first-person tüšije. Done: "I held"; note says the verb carries no person, why "I", and that it is a reading.
14. **U67 · `n` · moderate.** The note said "Sübeġetei is the name's first half as printed": false (it is printed whole; the Ming 速別額台 is the full name) and it invited the Sübegei confusion house-ruled in 195. Replaced with the house spelling remark. Also "The oldest-looking clause" (meaningless) → "hardest"; added that the ending of žüġegseġer(i)-jen may be -gsen + instrumental -ġer as in oluγsaγ̇ar, but the Ming gives no "according to", so left unanalysed.
15. **U71 · morph, `n` · moderate.** Lemma nököčel- + "-üġe" disagreed with the glossary (nököče-, from nökör) and left no parallel with keġeleġei / the glossary's kelelüġe (past -leġei/-lüġe, Ming 來). Done: nököče- + -lüġe "past ending (uncertain; Ming 來)", note amended; still marked a guess.
16. **`about` · moderate.** Said Chila'un, Chimbai, Badai and Kishiliq "share the rule of the spoils of war and the hunt": the rule of booty and hunt is given to Sorqan-Shira, Badai and Kishiliq (U37-39); Chila'un and Chimbai are told to name what they lack (U31-36). Corrected.

### Minor
17. **U31 · `n`.** Cited Ming 怎生 for ker; packet has 怎. Fixed.
18. **U35 · `n`.** "Three instrumentals" but only two are listed (öġer-ün bejes(i)-jer, ama-γ̇ar). Now "Two".
19. **U41 · `n`.** "A new speech of Chinggis" is an inference (no speaker is named); now "presumably Chinggis's". Also the note said the past ending is -γ̇ui while the morph (and glossary) split -žuγ̇ui; note now -žuγ̇ui.
20. **U52 · `i`, `n`; U58 · `n`.** "Biljiur" dropped the apostrophe the house gives γ̇ (Qada'an, Naya'a); now "Naya'a-Bilji'ur", with the note saying so.
21. **U53 · `l`.** `l` began with an opening quote mark that `t` and the packet do not have (idx 308 has none). Removed.
22. **U55 · `n`.** The note called ba the Ming's "exclusive we" against bida 咱, but the house (165-168; the glossary's bidan-dur) says the Ming alternates 俺/咱 for bida forms, so the Ming does not mark inclusive/exclusive. Reworded: the form leaves the listener out, the Ming does not show it.
23. **U62 · `n`.** "The first person is the Ming's": the Ming 說來 has no pronoun; the "I" rests on the first-person -je (Ming 咱). Reworded.
24. **U73 · `i`.** "stay (as one)": "(as one)" is not in the Ming (住您) and is covered by "together" in the previous word. Now "consulting together, stay,”.

## Findings refused (reason)
- **qorčila- "bow and quiver" (U27, U43)** — the Ming is 弓箭, "bow and arrows", but the shared glossary's qorčilaγ̇ulžu entry already says "bow and quiver (from qorči 'quiver-bearer')"; changing the unit would split from the house glossary. Left; glosser/owner to decide.
- **Γuowaṅ "prince of the state" (U64)** — 國王 is "king of a state", but the glossary and the 204-207 usage fix the wording; `i` keeps Guowang untranslated, as before. Left; flagged.
- **tebčin as noun, not tebči- + -n (U50, 54, 59, 60)** — the glossary treats tebčin as "giving up … form not analysed"; units follow it.
- **bida "inclusive" (U49)** — glossary says so; kept.
- **oroγ̇a "wild, cunning" (U39)** — the glossary lists both; the Ming here is 野 only, but the gloss is the house entry. Left.
- **U8 "When he had said this"** — "he" is To'oril by context; the word keġeġesü has no person. Left.
- **U63 dative on Boγ̇orču-da dropped in `i` ("Now, Bo'orchu:")** — Ming 行 on a name before 敎管者 is a marker I cannot assign to "to" or "as for"; `l` keeps "-to" and the note says dative-locative. Left.
- **U4, U6, U7, U10, U20, U22, U26, U34 (hedged readings)** — each rests on a guess the note already states as a guess; I found no better reading from the grammar and Ming alone, so they stand as uncertain.
- **U7 note "I think, the accusative" on deġü-jüġen** — hedged already; left.
- **Note unit numbers** — none given in this part's notes.

## Remaining doubts
1. U15: whether the sons are doers or accompanists (-jer ending shaped like the instrumental); Qada'an as the causee follows the accusative.
2. U46/U51: Shirgötü with sons Alaq and Naya'a, and why ta "you" also names Naya'a; the printed comma after Alaγ could also be read to group differently; and whether Širgötü is the Shirgügetü of earlier parts.
3. U49-U60: tebčižü barižu "casting aside, seizing"; the closing mark at ede" (U57) and the two words keġegdekün keġežüġü (U58) — whose words and whether inside the quote; the person of sedkižüġüi (U60).
4. U13/U14: who envies whom (aqa deġü-de, naitaγdamu).
5. U20 taγ̇alaqun and ambar; U24 medetügei "let him know" as "decide"; U26 "camp and all"; U32 böġesü after -dkün.
6. U4: the whole of the önöčid-ün clause.
7. U67 žüġegseġer(i)-jen ending; U68 bügdeġül; U71 nököčelüġe; U73 ejetüldüžü, adqun.
8. Glossary: tebčin / Γuowaṅ / qorčila- as above; the glosser should also broaden čeġeži-dür (胷膈 → also 心懷), and use naita-, darqan, dutaγ̇u, nököče- for the changed lemmas.

# Review, pass 2 — secret-history-218-223

Reviewer: adversarial, second pass. Files read: conventions.md, runbook.md, review.md (pass 1), units.json, gloss.json, novel-forms.json, known-forms.json, packet.md, the shared glossary. No modern translation, no web. Originals kept in the scratchpad (`units.p2orig.json`, `gloss.p2orig.json`). Both files edited in place by script (utf-8, ensure_ascii False, indent 1).

Re-checked by script: every `t` equals the packet words (73 units, 418 words, each once); `ln` and `p` correct; every first-morph Ming bracket equals the packet's Ming gloss (the only non-match is the l-a split, as intended); quote marks in `i` balance across the speeches (U13-20, 22-24, 26-28, 31-36, 37-39, 41-43, 46-57, 59-65, 70-73) and each supplied mark is said in a note. Read all 73 units again against the morphs; the pass-1 edits introduced no new error. Gloss: keys equal novel-forms keys exactly (58, none extra, none missing); every bracket equals the novel-forms Ming gloss (four had lost the U+FE00 mark, restored); all 15 `__broaden__` entries start with the old known-forms entry whole + ' · '.

Totals: 0 critical, 0 major, 5 moderate, 8 minor (units 2, gloss 22 entries rewritten, 8 broadenings added).

## Changes — units.json
1. **U2 · morph `-qu` · minor.** Gloss still read "about to, one who (fights)"; pass 1 removed "about to" from `i` and note because the Ming is 厮殺的 (not 要厮殺). Now "participle: one who (fights)".
2. **U46 · `n` · minor.** "the whole of §220 to the end of this part as Chinggis's speech" was wrong: Shiratori's printed mark closes it at ede (U57), and U59 reopens (supplied). Note now says so.

## Changes — gloss.json (entries rewritten)
Moderate:
3. **naitažu, naitaγdamu** — lemma naiti- → naita- (as the units and the glossary's naitamu).
4. **dataγ̇ui-ban, dutaγ̇u-juγ̇an** — lemma was an invented verb "dataγ̇u-/dutaγ̇u-"; now dutaγ̇u (adjective/participle from duta-), as the glossary and units; -i marked uncertain, not "participle".
5. **darqad** — lemma darqa(n) → darqan, with the glossary's darqad-un wording (no technical sense claimed).
6. **nököčelüġe** — nököčel- → nököče-, as the glossary's nököčesü/nököčežü.
7. **asaraγ̇ulžu** — "to look after, rear, raise up" with "having (them) raised" made the object plural and ignored the causative object; now "to lift, raise up, rear (Ming 擡擧; here 'tend, bring up')", "having (someone) tend (him)", following the glossary's asaraba "lift, raise up" and pass 1's reading of U15.
Minor:
8. **kičiġežü** — "be diligent" → "be careful (Ming 謹愼 'careful')", as the unit.
9. **neküs** — removed the unsupported "(Nököd?)" identification and "plural-looking"; kept "perhaps a plural".
10. **buratara** — removed the speculative "converb/participle of a verb 'to scatter'" to "perhaps a converb; uncertain".
11. **čiγ̇ulγa** — "ending lost" was wrong: the ending is the next token (-suγai); said so.
12. **čaγan-γoγ̇a** — dropped "as a woman's name elsewhere" (no such entry in the glossary); γoγ̇a taken from the glossary ("name element Qo'a").
13. **narin-toγ̇ori, l-a** — wording only (the name's last letter is on the next line).
14. **taγ̇alaqun** — "to be fond of, like" → "to like, be fond of" (glossary taγ̇alan "to like").
15. **seleṅge-ji** — "(Ming 地名)" now says the Ming gives only "place name" (the glossary's Seleṅge has 水名).
16. **γuiqun, γuidqun** — "beg" → "ask for, claim", as the glossary's γui-.
17. **keleledkün** — added the use after bu ("do not tell", U34).
18. **tarqutai, kiriltug-i** — dictionary forms now Tarqutai-Kiriltuγ / Kiriltuγ, matching the units' lemma.
19. **γartažu** — "set to work" dropped (Ming 下手 "set hand to"; the sense in context is "laying hands on").
20. **datuγdažu** — tied to dutaγ̇u/duta- "lacking", said the vowels differ; still uncertain.
21. **ažuγ̇ui-že, kičiġežü, alaγdaluγ̇a, abtuγai** — Ming brackets had lost U+FE00; restored to the novel-forms string.
22. The rest (čaγan-γoγ̇a-jin, sorγan-šira-da, najaγ̇a-da, širgötü, tan-luγ̇a, tödege-ji, qandaqu, aldal-dur, oġer-ün, öġesüd, darqalasu, darqaladqun, darqalarun, bariγ̇asu, udaγ̇an-a, abtuγai, itegegdekün, keġegdekün, sedkižüġüi, tüšije, medeġülbe, tüb-ün, oluγsad, žüġegseġeri, qoniči-da, bügdeġül-i, modoči-da, žüki-jer, üile-dür, najaγ̇a-bilžiγ̇ur, tarqutai-kiril, tug-i, γartaγsad, alaγdaluγ̇a, ažuγ̇ui-že) checked against form, morphs and Ming: unchanged.

## Changes — `__broaden__`
Pass-1's instruction applied: čeġeži-dür carries 心懷 (with the cross-reference to the glossary's čeġeži 胷懷); the glosser's seven broadenings kept with their tails tightened to name the construction (darqalan, qaγ̇ulžu, qubčižu, čeġeži-dür, gegeġen, že, abalaγ̇asu). Added eight known forms whose entry does not cover this part's use:
- **qadqulduqu** (entry "about to fight" [要厮殺]; here Ming 厮殺的, "one who fights").
- **tutum** (entry "each", 各各/每遍; here 每裏 after qari).
- **jen** (no sedkil(i)-, sedkigsen(i)-, žüġegseġer(i)- among its contexts).
- **talbižu** (entry "set down, leave"; here "let go, set free", 放着/放了着).
- **ügüledkün** (entry imperative only; U32 "if you say" before böġesü, Ming 說的每).
- **bejesi** (entry assumes -jen; here before -jer, Ming 親身(每)敎).
- **jer** (no bejes(i)-jer among its contexts).
- **keġeleġei** (entry "past question [說來麽]"; here Ming 說來 without 麽, plain past).
Checked and left alone (entry covers the use, Ming variants only): köġün, ečige, deġü forms, uruγ-un, kürtele, aqu, ta, žeġüdün-dür, γažar, merkid-ün, medetügei (both senses present), ba (both senses), qojar forms, jan (already lists qān(i)-), odqun, irebe, nigen(-e), ede, jadaγsan, minγalažu, adqun, and the rest of the 202.

## Findings refused (reason)
- **qorčila- "bow and quiver" (U27, U43)** — carried from pass 1: the glossary's qorčilaγ̇ulžu says so; unit/gloss follow it. Owner to decide.
- **Γuowaṅ gloss "prince of the state"** — the glossary's entry; the gloss.json had no entry for it (known form), so nothing to align.
- **Lemma datuγda- (U70)** — kept as the unit's lemma although the glossary's duta- "to be lacking" (dutaba) probably underlies it: the Ming 被缺着 and the form do not decide, so the uncertainty is in the entry rather than a forced change.
- **tebčin as a noun, bida "inclusive" (U49), oroγ̇a "wild, cunning" (U39)** — the glossary's wording; left.
- **U41 "We were people of Tödöge"** — the "we" is flagged in the note as supplied; kept.
- **U58 keġegdekün keġežüġü / U57 mark at ede** — already hedged in the notes; no better reading.

## Remaining doubts
1. U15 (Qada'an as causee), U46/U51 (grouping of Širgötü, Alaq, Naya'a with ta), U49-U60 (tebčižü barižu; whose words keġegdekün keġežüġü are; person of sedkižüġüi), U13/U14 (who envies whom).
2. U20 taγ̇alaqun/ambar; U24 medetügei; U26 "camp and all"; U32 ügüledkün before böġesü; U4 önöčid-ün clause.
3. U67 žüġegseġer(i)-jen ending; U68 bügdeġül; U70 datuγda-; U71 nököčelüġe; U73 ejetüldüžü, adqun.
4. Glossary-level, for the owner: qorčila-, Γuowaṅ, tebčin; Širgötü vs Shirgügetü; the glossary's čeġeži-dür (胷膈) and čeġeži (胷懷) now differ from each other and from this part's 心懷, which the broadening records.
